claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18's logic matches its specification and has no defect; however, the regression test did not exercise carrier scheduling, leaving an untested integration point
claims.corroboration: Verified from inventory_control replay review at trust_tier 1
claims.limitation: Confirms rule logic is correct; the defect must be in how carriers handle the split-reservation pattern generated by v18

claims.statement: The root cause is a carrier feed lag or scheduling incompatibility on the east-node lanes, triggered by v18's split-reservation pattern which was not tested with carrier scheduling
claims.corroboration: Rule logic verified correct; 100% correlation of held orders with v18 split-reservations routed to east node; carrier scheduling not tested; no other node affected
claims.limitation: Must still identify which specific carrier feed is affected and confirm the lag; dock capacity must be checked to rule out physical space constraints

next_action.rationale: We have narrowed the root cause to carrier-side issues (carrier_feed_lag or scheduling incompatibility) based on v18 rule verification. Checking dock capacity at the east node will determine whether the 186 held orders are physically constrained at the dock (indicating dock_capacity issue) or whether the problem is carrier feed lag / pickup scheduling. If dock capacity is adequate, it confirms carrier_feed_lag/pickup scheduling is the bottleneck, which would support the root_cause claim and allow progression to mitigation.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Will discriminate between physical dock capacity constraint vs. carrier feed lag / pickup scheduling issue. If capacity is adequate, establishes carrier_feed_lag as definitive root cause.
